idea-plugin.name: IntelliCursor
idea-plugin.description:
Chat with the Cursor agent inside IntelliJ IDEA. IntelliCursor connects to the Cursor CLI you already have installed and gives it a chat panel in the IDE, so you can ask questions, plan changes and let the agent edit your project without switching to a terminal.

Features

  • Chat panel: your messages on the right, Cursor's replies on the left, with live progress while it thinks, runs tools and writes.
  • Attach files with @: search your project and add files to a message.
  • Commands with /: new chat, resume, summarize, switch between Agent, Plan and Ask modes, choose a model, review changes, commit, and your Cursor skills and custom commands.
  • Chat history: reopen and continue any earlier chat in the project.
  • MCP servers: see each server's status, turn it on or off, sign in, and list its tools.
  • Approvals: review each file edit or shell command before it runs, or turn on Run everything to approve them all.
  • Editor actions: send, explain or refactor the selected code from the editor's right-click menu, and review the agent's edits in the IntelliJ diff viewer.

Requirements

  • The Cursor CLI (agent), installed and signed in. Install it with curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash.
  • A Cursor account.

Getting started

  1. Open the IntelliCursor tool window from the right-hand stripe, or View | Tool Windows | IntelliCursor.
  2. If the header says Signed out, click Sign in and finish the login in your browser.
  3. Pick a mode (Agent, Plan or Ask) and a model under the message box, type a message and press Enter.
  4. Type @ to attach project files, or / to see all commands. The file open in the editor is attached automatically.
  5. When Cursor wants to edit a file or run a command, choose Allow Once, Allow Always or Deny.
  6. Type /changes to review the agent's edits in the diff viewer, and /commit to commit them.

You can also select code in the editor, right-click and choose IntelliCursor to send, explain or refactor it.

Source code, documentation and issues: github.com/ceasle/IntelliCursor

IntelliCursor is an independent project. It is not made or endorsed by Cursor or Anysphere.
